paper.title: Intergenerational Health Mobility: Evidence from Danish Registers
paper.code_data_availability: No data- or code-availability statement and no Statistics Denmark project number is given. …

registers.name_in_paper: Danish register data provided by Statistics Denmark
registers.role: sample frame and linkage; all registers carry a unique personal identifier allowing links to parents and across registers
inputs to the health measure for both generations: binary indicators of ever having been registered with each diagnosis category
variables_mentioned: individual level inpatient and outpatient hospital contacts and the duration of the stay
23-category aggregation of International Classification of Diseases (ICD) used by Statistics Denmark (Statistics Denmark (2011), 'Diag23')

registers.name_in_paper: general practitioner visits (GP visits, also referred to as doctor visits)
registers.role: inputs to the health measure for both generations: indicators for quintiles of the number of GP visits
sample restriction (parents neither dead nor emigrated by age 70; children alive by age 50) and validation of the health measure in Appendix A
validation of the child health measure in Appendix A (disability-pension uptake in the age interval 46-50)

linkages: All Danish registers contain a unique personal identifier allowing the author to link individuals to parents and across different registers
Siblings are defined as individuals who share a biological mother and a biological father (in very few cases the definition will instead capture only the social father)

Twins are identified in the data but zygosity is not observed; monozygotic twin correlations are identified by the Nicoletti and Rabe (2013) / Bjorklund and Jantti (2012) procedure using mixed-sex twins

sample.universe: Danish children born 1960-1963 with parents born 1930-1940; the sample is stated to be representative of the Danish population and to constitute more than 95 percent of the population in the child cohorts
sample.unit_of_observation: individual child (son or daughter), linked to each parent and, for the correlation analyses, to siblings and twins within the family
selection_rules: Select children born between 1960-1963 with parents born 1930-1940 (71,460 children)
Keep children whose parents are neither dead nor emigrated by age 70
Measure child health over ages 36-50 (14 years) and parental health over ages 60-70 (10 years)
Estimate separately for sons and daughters, and separately against fathers and mothers
For sibling correlations: siblings share a biological mother and a biological father; non-twin siblings, twins and (identified) monozygotic twins are treated as separate blocks
Appendix C restricts to child birth cohort 1960 and measures parental health at ages 60-65
Appendix D excludes GP visits from the health measure and excludes the twin estimations
sample.n_individuals: 36,178 sons from 32,674 families and 35,282 daughters from 31,983 families; 58,535 unique fathers and 58,609 unique mothers; 444 male twins, 446 female twins and 430 mixed sex twins. Appendix C cohort-1960 sample: 8,731 sons and 8,658 daughters.

construction_notes: Health is measured as the first principal component ('pca' in Stata 14) of binary hospital diagnosis-category indicators and indicators of GP-visit quintiles; the first component explains 13-14 percent of the overall variability
Hospital indicators record whether the individual has ever been registered in inpatient or outpatient care with the given ailment over the observation window; they are binary, not counts

All diagnosis categories of the Statistics Denmark 23-category ICD aggregation are included apart from sterilisations, poisonings and concussions, and apart from explicitly gender related categories such as pregnancy complications and gynecological conditions; Table 1 lists the 14 retained categories
All outcome variables are net of cohort effects; all results are net of cohort fixed effects and presented by gender
For rank-rank specifications individuals are assigned a percentile rank within each cohort and gender according to their predicted value of the first principal component
The intergenerational correlation is the slope standardized by the ratio of parent to child standard deviations, gamma = (sigmaP/sigmaC) beta (equation (2))
Sibling correlations are variance components (equations (4)-(6)) estimated by REML with standard errors bootstrapped using 100 replications
Monozygotic twin correlations impose regularity conditions on the variance components because zygosity is unobserved (Nicoletti and Rabe, 2013; Bjorklund and Jantti, 2012)

Appendix D alternative measures: a 'simple fractions' measure (number of hospital categories the individual has been associated with divided by 14) and a principal component of the same hospital indicators, both excluding GP visits

Appendix A validates the health measure against four-year mortality (parents at ages 70-74) and disability-pension uptake and mortality (children at ages 46-50); for that exercise child health is computed over ages 36-46
